questions.text: Two hosts are connected via a packet switch with [latex]10^{7}[/latex] bits per second links. Each link has a propagation delay of 20 microseconds. The switch begins forwarding a packet 35 microseconds after it receives the same. If 10000 bits of data are to be transmitted between the two hosts using a packet size of 5000 bits, the time elapsed between the transmission of the first bit of data and the reception of the last bit of the data in microseconds is____________.
questions.solution:
Each packet: [latex]T_t=\frac{5000}{10^7}=500\,\mu s[/latex], propagation 20 [latex]\mu s[/latex], switch delay 35 [latex]\mu s[/latex].

- Packet 1: sent 0-500, at switch by 520, forwarded 555-1055, received by 1075
- Packet 2: sent 500-1000, at switch by 1020, forwarded 1055-1555, received by 1575

Answer: 1575

questions.text: For the processes listed in the following table, which of the following scheduling schemes will give the lowest average turnaround time?
questions.solution:
Average turnaround time:

- FCFS: A 0-3, B 3-9, C 9-13, D 13-15 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (3 + 8 + 9 + 9)/4 = 7.25
- Non-preemptive SJF: A, B, D, C [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (3 + 8 + 5 + 11)/4 = 6.75
- SRT: A 0-3, B 3-4, C 4-8, D 8-10, B 10-15 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (3 + 14 + 4 + 4)/4 = 6.25
- RR (q = 2) is higher than SRT

Answer: Shortest Remaining Time

questions.text:
Consider three software items: Program-X, Control Flow Diagram of Program-Y and Control Flow Diagram of Program-Z as shown below

The values of McCabe's Cyclomatic complexity of Program-X, Program-Y, and Program-Z respectively are
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Program X: decisions are if, while and if-else [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3 + 1 = 4
- Program Y: 8 nodes, 7 forward edges + 3 back edges = 10 edges [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10 [latex]-[/latex] 8 + 2 = 4
- Program Z: X followed by Y, joined by one edge [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 + 4 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 7

Answer: 4, 4, 7

questions.text: Consider the equation [latex](43)_{x}=(y3)_{8}[/latex] where x and y are unknown. The number of possible solutions is ______________
questions.solution:
[latex](43)_x=4x+3,\quad(y3)_8=8y+3\Rightarrow x=2y[/latex]

Digit 4 needs x [latex]\ge[/latex] 5 and y must be an octal digit (0 to 7). So y = 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 solutions.

Answer: 5

questions.text: Let R be a relation on the set of ordered pairs of positive integers such that [latex]((p,q),(r,s)) \in R[/latex] if and only if [latex]p-s=q-r[/latex]. Which one of the following is true about R?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Reflexive needs p [latex]-[/latex] q = q [latex]-[/latex] p, i.e. p = q. Fails for (1, 2) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not reflexive.
- Symmetric: ((r,s),(p,q)) needs r [latex]-[/latex] q = s [latex]-[/latex] p, which rearranges to p [latex]-[/latex] s = q [latex]-[/latex] r [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] symmetric.

Answer: Not reflexive but symmetric
